findings.summary: Section 3 diagram labels are fragmentary, and the final line mentions the raw form without explaining it.
findings.evidence: "Only the raw and wildcard forms relate List<Integer> and List<Number>."
findings.fix: Show a diagram of Integer extends Number with List<Integer> and List<Number> as unrelated siblings, and List<? extends Number> as their common supertype. Drop the raw-type mention here, since raw types are covered on page 5.

findings.summary: The generic method bullet is vague and shows code before the idea is stated.
findings.evidence: "Generic method: own parameter before the return type" followed by the java block, with the "T is usually inferred" bullet in between.
findings.fix: State the one-line idea first, as in '<T> goes before the return type; T is inferred from the arguments'. Then show the code.

findings.summary: The wildcard table is inconsistent and ambiguous. The note '(compile error)' sits inside a Write cell, and the 'Read gives' column for super is 'Object' while the Write column is OK.
findings.evidence: "List<? extends Number> | Number | only null (compile error)"
findings.fix: Write 'null only' in every Write cell, and add a separate note that adding any non-null element to ? extends is a compile error.

findings.summary: The bullet '? extends = producer: read-only' conflates the role with the access mode, and '? super = consumer: write-friendly' is loose. Each bullet holds two ideas.
findings.fix: Split the bullets, or move the role into the table's role column as page 6 does.

findings.summary: The Reified vs Erased table has a vague 'n/a' cell. The 'Reifiable lists' row mixes in non-array facts, so its column comparison is meaningless.
findings.evidence: "Reifiable lists | n/a | only List<?> and raw List"
findings.fix: Replace the row with 'Reifiable types | all array types | only unbounded wildcard and raw forms'.

findings.summary: Terminology is inconsistent for the same failure. Page 3 says the 'inserted cast', page 4 says 'the cast to T checks nothing' and 'unchecked cast', and the two uses of ClassCastException are not tied together.
findings.evidence: "The ClassCastException comes later, at the inserted cast" and "A cast to T checks nothing"
findings.fix: Use one term, such as 'compiler-inserted cast at the call site' for the failing cast and 'unchecked cast (T)' for the no-op cast, and define each once.

findings.summary: The chapter says throwing a value of type T is illegal, but it is legal when T extends Throwable.
findings.evidence: catch (T e) and throw of T: illegal
findings.fix: Say only catch (T e) is illegal. Also say a generic class cannot extend Throwable. Throwing a T that is bounded by Throwable, and declaring `throws T`, are allowed.

findings.summary: The Runtime Type Workarounds section shows a long code block, while the idea of using a Class<T> token for construction is only one line. The TypeToken bullet is cryptic.
findings.evidence: "TypeToken: anonymous subclass keeps List<String> in its superclass"
findings.fix: Explain TypeToken in a plain sentence, such as 'new TypeToken<List<String>>(){} stores the type argument in the subclass signature, so reflection can read it'. Keep the code short.

findings.summary: The first bullet of the bans section packs several unrelated bans together, and the static-field bullet is unclear.
findings.evidence: "new T(), new T[10], T.class: T is gone at runtime" and "static T field: one static shared by every Box<X>"
findings.fix: Present the bans as a table with columns Banned | Why.

findings.summary: The code is shown before its idea in the raw types section, and the sample comments are cryptic ('CCE' is never defined).
findings.fix: Spell out ClassCastException, and put the one-line idea ahead of the code.

findings.summary: Page 5 title casing is inconsistent ('Raw types', 'Generic arrays'), and the section 3 varargs bullets mix several ideas.
findings.fix: Split the bullets into one idea each: where @SafeVarargs is allowed, and what it promises.
